title: Abandonment of an Unpaid Order and the Refund Window
content:
1. A Lift Tickets order not yet paid for may be abandoned against the product's abandonment fee.

2. A paid order may be given back only where the product's refund basis allows it, and only when the refund is asked for no later than the product's refund window counted in calendar days from the day the order was recorded. Both conditions hold together: a product whose basis does not allow a refund gives nothing back however early the request comes, and a product whose basis does allow one gives nothing back on a request later than its window.

3. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used.

4. The anchor date for condition 2 is the day the order was recorded, as the order's own record shows it, and the last day of the window is itself within the window.

## What each of the two dispositions leaves behind

An order stands cancelled where the household abandoned it before paying for it. An order stands refunded where the household gave up a paid order before any media was issued, gave up an issued order before any day was scanned, or gave up the days still unused on a part-used order.

## The window worked through

Suppose a refund window of 10 calendar days and an order recorded on 2026-12-05, both figures taken for this illustration. The day the order was recorded is day zero, and counting forward 10 calendar days, weekdays and weekend days counting alike, the window closes on 2026-12-15. A refund asked for on 2026-12-15 is no later than the window; one asked for on 2026-12-16 is later than it. Where such a count would land on a date the target month does not hold, the last day of that month is used.
